title: Perf Canary Rollout Checklist (per region)
content:
Purpose
- This is the eng-releases checklist for enabling the perf-canary per region/tier, verifying dashboards + alert routing, and confirming rollback/disable hooks.
- Goal: detect p95 latency regressions and tokens/sec drops per model with minimal noise and <0.5% GPU overhead per region.

Owner + escalation
- Release owner (DRI): eng-releases oncall (assign in #eng-releases)
- Runtime DRI: Noah Patel (perf canary TL)
- SRE DRI: Rafael Mendes (routing + paging)
- Telemetry DRI: Logan Wright / Nadia Rahman
- Infra/fleet DRI: Vanessa Ortiz

Definitions (for this checklist)
- “Enable canary” = deploy perf-canary workload + emit metrics + dashboards show data.
- “Enable warning alerts” = warning-level rules live, routed to #eng-runtime, no pages.
- “Enable paging” = paging rules live (Sev2/Sev1), routed to oncall rotation + #eng-oncall.
- “Gates” = release engineering automation that can pause or block rollout based on canary signal.

Pre-flight (do once per release train)
[ ] Confirm change window: no overlapping high-risk runtime kernel/scheduler changes beyond what’s in the release plan.
[ ] Confirm canary service account + scope is least-privilege and valid in target region.
    - Must be able to: call internal inference endpoints (read-only), write metrics, write traces (if configured), read baseline artifacts.
[ ] Confirm control-plane config surface is working for canary model list + threshold config.
    - Validate config audit logging is enabled.
[ ] Confirm capacity budget/QPS caps are set to safe defaults.
    - Target: <0.5% GPU overhead per region for covered models.
    - Ensure guardrails exist to prevent accidental wide fanout (region x model x tier explosion).
[ ] Confirm baseline artifacts exist for target region/SKU/model set.
    - Baseline keys must include: model + model_version + runtime_build + hardware_sku (+ region if configured).
    - Minimum sample size documented for baseline validity.
[ ] Confirm dashboards exist and are accessible to eng-runtime + SRE.
    - Grafana: per-model latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens/sec, prefill/decode/queueing breakdown, batch size distribution.
[ ] Confirm incident-bot handler is deployed and dedupe keys are correct.
    - Dedupe key must include: model, model_version, region, tier, signal_type (latency vs tps), runtime_build (optional if it helps).
[ ] Confirm runbook link in alert payload is correct and publicly accessible internally.

Per-region rollout steps (repeat for each region)
Region: ____________   Tier(s): ____________   Hardware SKU(s): ____________
Models to enable (start small): ____________

1) Deployment + config
[ ] Confirm Helm values for this region are correct:
    - region=<region>
    - tiers enabled (hosted/dedicated/private as applicable)
    - hardware_sku dimension enabled only if intended
    - qps cap set (documented) + capacity budget enabled
    - logging redaction/no-PII assertions enabled
[ ] Apply Terraform/IAM changes if needed for the region.
[ ] Deploy/upgrade perf-canary chart in the region.
    - Note release version/tag: ____________
[ ] Apply control-plane config: canary target model list for region/tier.
    - Confirm config validation passes (no unexpected wildcarding).
[ ] Confirm baseline lookup succeeds for each model entry.
    - If baseline missing: STOP and create baseline (or mark model out-of-scope for this region).

2) Smoke test (before looking at dashboards)
[ ] Canary is producing requests (steady state) without elevated errors.
[ ] Inference endpoints are not showing elevated 429s/5xx attributable to canary traffic.
[ ] Canary logs show:
    - model + version resolved correctly
    - runtime build tag present
    - kernel selection tag present (if applicable)
    - scheduler queueing metrics present
[ ] Canary emits metrics with expected label set (cardinality check):
    - Allowed: model, model_version, region, tier, runtime_build, hardware_sku (if explicitly enabled)
    - Not allowed: prompt_id, request_id, customer_id, any free-form strings

3) Dashboard verification
[ ] Open per-model dashboard and confirm data appears within expected ingestion latency.
[ ] Verify these panels populate for each model enabled:
    - End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99
    - Runtime-only latency p50/p95/p99
    - Tokens/sec
    - Prefill latency + decode latency
    - Queueing time
    - Batch size distribution
    - (Optional) KV cache hit rate (if enabled)
[ ] Sanity check values vs baseline:
    - Not expecting “green” immediately; expecting “reasonable” and stable.
    - If off by >~20% immediately, check:
        - wrong hardware SKU
        - wrong model version
        - accidental cross-region routing
        - queueing time inflated due to mis-sized canary concurrency

4) Warning alerts enablement (recommended first)
[ ] Confirm warning alert rules are deployed for the region/model set.
[ ] Confirm routing to #eng-runtime (and not paging).
[ ] Confirm alert payload contains:
    - model + model_version + region + tier
    - observed vs baseline values (p95 and/or tps)
    - confidence/min sample size indicator
    - links: dashboard + traces/logs + runbook
[ ] Confirm anti-flap / dampening:
    - minimum sample size condition enforced
    - sustain window (e.g., 10–15 min) enforced
    - cooldown/dedupe window enforced

5) Paging enablement (only after 3–7 days stable warnings)
Do NOT enable paging on day 0 unless explicitly approved by SRE sponsor.
[ ] Confirm paging rules are scoped to:
    - top models (or explicitly approved high-risk models)
    - sustained regressions only
[ ] Confirm paging route is correct:
    - oncall rotation + #eng-oncall + #eng-runtime
[ ] Confirm incident-bot dedupe works (no duplicate pages for same ongoing regression).
[ ] Confirm “silence” workflow exists (how to mute paging if telemetry breaks).

6) Rollback + disable hooks (must be verified per region)
[ ] Verify canary has a safe-disable switch.
    - Disable should stop request generation without impacting inference endpoints.
    - Document mechanism (feature flag / config / scale-to-zero): ____________
[ ] Verify rollback of perf-canary deployment:
    - Helm rollback path tested (chart version N-1 works)
    - Terraform changes are reversible (or forward-fix only; document if so)
[ ] Verify rollout gate integration (if enabled in this region):
    - Gate signal source is canary (not customer traffic)
    - Gate behavior is documented (auto-pause vs notify-only)
    - Clear owner to unpause after triage
[ ] Verify runtime rollback automation hooks are reachable:
    - If canary indicates runtime regression, releases can pause further rollout and/or trigger rollback runbook.
    - Confirm runbook includes exact commands/steps for runtime rollback in this region.

7) Sign-offs (required to expand coverage)
[ ] Runtime sign-off (Noah or delegate): metrics look correct + attribution signals present.
[ ] SRE sign-off (Rafael or delegate): paging hygiene acceptable (if paging enabled).
[ ] Telemetry sign-off (Logan/Nadia): cardinality + ingestion latency acceptable.
[ ] Infra/fleet sign-off (Vanessa or delegate): overhead within budget, no noisy neighbor impact.

Expansion checklist (after initial region success)
When adding models or expanding to another region:
[ ] Expand model list incrementally (e.g., +2–3 models/day).
[ ] Verify each added model has a baseline for the region/SKU.
[ ] For each new model, validate:
    - label cardinality remains bounded
    - dashboards populate
    - warning alerts fire only when expected (no immediate storm)
[ ] Confirm region-specific thresholds if variance differs (do not copy/paste blindly).

Common stop-ship conditions (release freeze triggers)
If any of the below occur, STOP expansion and loop in #eng-releases + runtime + SRE:
- Canary overhead exceeds budget and can’t be reduced quickly (risking customer impact)
- Alert storm due to baseline drift/cardinality/telemetry lag
- Sustained p95 regression on a top model with high confidence
- Tokens/sec drop sustained beyond threshold on top model or a key Dedicated pool
- Telemetry ingestion delays cause late/incorrect alerting (cannot trust signal)

Notes / per-region record (fill during rollout)
- Region: ____________
- Date enabled (metrics only): ____________
- Date warning alerts enabled: ____________
- Date paging enabled: ____________
- Models enabled: ____________
- Runtime build(s): ____________
- Hardware SKU(s): ____________
- Any deviations from standard policy (and approver): ____________

Appendix: Quick triage pointers (for releases)
- If queueing time spikes but runtime-only latency is flat: likely scheduler/capacity/traffic mix issue.
- If runtime-only latency spikes + kernel tag changed: likely kernel regression or kernel auto-selection.
- If tokens/sec drops but latency unchanged: check batch sizing, kv cache behavior, or GPU clock/fleet changes.
- If only one region regresses: check fleet change, driver, GPU SKU drift, or regional routing.

Last updated
- 2026-02-10 (Connor): incorporate post-alert-storm changes: stricter min-samples, tighter dedupe guidance, and explicit paging go/no-go gating.
